title: Podcastle Pricing 2026: Plans, Limits & What You Get
summary: Podcastle pricing offers four plans separated by monthly allowance and output quality. Determine which limits you'll hit first to find your best fit.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is Podcastle really free?


Yes, Podcastle has a free plan, but it's a capped one. You can record and edit, and the limits on recording hours, transcription, AI credits and export quality are where you'll feel the ceiling.


If the first limit you hit is one you can't work around, that's your signal to move up.


### Does Podcastle offer a free trial or refunds?


Since you can run a real episode through it before paying anything, the free plan works as the trial.


Refund terms are a different matter. They are set in Podcastle's billing terms and can change, and I have no confirmed wording to quote, so read the current terms on its pricing and legal pages before committing to an annual payment.


### Can I switch plans or cancel anytime?


You manage Podcastle subscriptions from your account settings, so changing or cancelling doesn't require contacting anyone.


What I can't confirm is exactly how a mid-cycle change is prorated or when access ends after cancelling. That detail decides whether upgrading for one heavy month is cheap or wasteful.


If you're upgrading for a single batch of episodes, check how the change is billed first, and note the renewal date so a plan you meant to drop doesn't renew.


### Is there a discount for annual billing or students?


Annual billing is typically cheaper per month than paying monthly, and Podcastle's pricing page shows the current comparison for each plan.


The trade-off is commitment: an annual plan locks you in before you know which limit you'll hit first. If you're still unsure, pay monthly for a cycle or two, then switch once your usage pattern is clear.


I have no confirmed information on a student discount, so check the pricing page, or ask support, rather than assuming one exists.


### Does Podcastle have an API or integrations?


Podcastle is built as a browser-based studio for recording and editing, and I have no confirmed details of a public API. Don't plan an automated pipeline around one.


If your workflow depends on programmatic uploads, transcript retrieval or hands-off publishing, verify what Podcastle documents today before youratchet a plan. Otherwise assume the practical route is manual: export your finished audio or transcript and carry it into your hosting or publishing tools yourself.
